title: Experiment 1 Lab Manual
description:
Straight Line Motion with Constant Velocity
Exp. ME-1
Purpose
The purpose of this experiment is to verify that a puck on which no net force acts moves in a straight line
with constant velocity, and to find that velocity in two ways, from the slope of its x-t graph and from its
average velocity between two dots, and compare the results.
Introduction
By Newton’s first law, a body on which no net force acts moves in a straight line with constant velocity.
On a level air table gravity does not pull the puck along the table, and the air cushion removes almost
all friction, so a puck that is pushed and released should move this way.
Take the x-axis along the puck’s path, in the direction it moves. Its velocity then has only an x-
component, written simply as v, which is positive and equal to the speed. A puck moving with constant
velocity v from position x0 at t = 0 is at time t at
x(t) = x0 + v t. (1.1)
With the origin at the puck’s position at t = 0, x0 = 0 and a graph of x against t is a straight line through
the origin with slope v, as in Fig. 1.1.
